The original: NIFTY 50 market filter, 0.5R time stop
notes: Entry: monthly StochRSI pullback; close above EMA 61 on monthly, weekly and daily; RSI above 50; NIFTY 500 index above its 200-day average (previous close).

Exits: stop at the previous week's low; sell at the next open if the trade is not 0.25R up 25 days after entry; otherwise hold until the weekly Supertrend(10, 3) turns from bullish to bearish after entry (sold at the next open). A trade bought while it is already bearish is held until it turns bullish and then bearish, or until the stop or time stop. No holding cap.

Sizing: 1% risk per trade on current equity, 10 slots; no position above 20% of equity when bought, and trimmed to 20% at month end; halve size at a 10% drawdown, pause 21 days at 15%. Idle cash in a liquid fund. No NIFTY futures hedges.
The worst drawdown (May–June 2006 crash) can't be cut by an entry filter; plan for about −25% to −30%. Expect long losing streaks (29 in a row in the backtest): about 1 trade in 4 wins.

notes: SQN 1.9 on Tharp's 100-trade basis (1.6–1.9 poor but tradable, 2–2.4 average, 2.5–2.9 good, 3–5 excellent); 3.8 on all 410 trades. Expectancy +2.32R, std dev of R 12.3R. Sa1f19d11: SQN 2.0, expectancy +2.53R.
Low SQN, high expectancy: a few huge winners (best 137R) widen the R spread. Without the 10 best trades expectancy is +0.61R, still positive; missing big winners is the main risk.

Market types: bull days and quiet sideways days earn almost all the R; volatile sideways markets are the bleed (negative expectancy), and the NIFTY 500 filter keeps the strategy mostly out of bear markets (few trades, near-flat returns).

Each day typed from NIFTY 50 up to the previous close: 13-week change above +5% bull, below −5% bear; volatile if 20-day volatility is above its rolling 3-year median. Trades filed by their entry day.
